themes.name: Critical Thinking Enhancement through AI
themes.definition: The integration of artificial intelligence tools in educational contexts to develop, improve, or assess students' critical thinking skills, as explicitly stated in multiple studies across various disciplines.
evidence: [Abdulayeva2025] The system fostered improved critical thinking, research competencies, and self-assessment skills
[Syahri2025] the AI-supported PBL model is considered valid, highly practical, and effective in enhancing the critical thinking abilities
[Xiaolei2024] the findings emphasized the pivotal roles of critical thinking skills and self-directed learning in AI-assisted writing

themes.name: AI-Integrated Educational Frameworks
themes.definition: The development and implementation of structured learning models or frameworks that incorporate artificial intelligence to enhance educational processes and outcomes, such as Problem-Based Learning or design thinking approaches.
evidence: [Syahri2025] AI-PBL Framework: Innovative Problem Based Learning Model Supported by Artificial Intelligence Technology
[Lee2025b] a design thinking-based generative AI education program
[Chen2025d] a GenAI-empowered, group-based authentic assessment for a Network Engineering course

themes.name: Metacognition and Self-Directed Learning
themes.definition: The use of artificial intelligence to promote metacognitive awareness, self-reflection, and autonomous learning capabilities among students, often through prompts or tailored feedback.
evidence: [Chen2025c] GenAI played a dual role in metacognition of design: it not only propelled design actions, but also created opportunities for reflection
[Singh2025a] metacognitive prompts—designed to encourage people to pause, reflect, assess their understanding, and consider multiple perspectives
[Lowry2025] leveraging generative artificial intelligence to cultivate metacognition and promote readiness for self-directed learning

themes.name: Domain-Specific Skill Enhancement
themes.definition: The application of artificial intelligence tools to improve specific competencies such as writing, language proficiency, or technical skills in various academic and professional domains, as observed in studies focusing on language learning, engineering, and other fields.
evidence: [Rodomanchenko2024] the introduction of generative AI tools in the Business English language course had a positive impact on students' writing proficiency, language fluency, and critical thinking skills
[Yuan2024] the most notable improvement is in students' critical thinking abilities during English reading
[Cigerci2025] students showed marked improvement in productive language skills (speaking and writing)

themes.name: Ethical and Practical Considerations of AI Use
themes.definition: Discussions on the potential risks, challenges, and need for balanced approaches when integrating AI into education, including concerns about over-reliance, misinformation, and cognitive impacts, as highlighted in several studies.
evidence: [Derakhshan2025] AI serves as a double-edged sword, capable of both fostering and impeding the development of higher-order thinking skills
[Farinetti2024] the well-known risk of generative AI for potential misinformation offers fertile ground to practice critical thinking
[Balá2024] it may also detract from deep understanding and critical thinking, as evidenced by the uniformity and superficial engagement in solutions

themes.name: Personalized and Adaptive Learning
themes.definition: AI-driven systems that tailor educational content, feedback, or prompts to individual learner needs, performance, or learning styles, as described in studies focusing on personalised learning approaches.
evidence: [Abdulayeva2025] AI-driven personalised learning system designed to adapt content based on student performance
[Li2025e] RGPT provides personalized reflective prompts at each stage of inquiry

[Zhu2025] Oliver, an innovative virtual teaching assistant and course management system that leverages contextual memory and response strategies designed to promote active learning and critical thinking

themes.name: Student Engagement and Motivation
themes.definition: The enhancement of student involvement, interest, and active participation through the use of artificial intelligence tools in learning activities, as reported in studies measuring engagement, satisfaction, or motivation.
evidence: [Rolf2025] students perceived that this experiential learning exercise effectively promoted student engagement
[Cigerci2025] AI-supported P4C increased students' attention, motivation, and participation

[Elizondo-García2025] the perception survey revealed high satisfaction levels, with average ratings exceeding nine on a 10-point scale for dimensions such as usefulness, engagement, and learning relevance

data.meta_observations: Critical thinking is a dominant and recurring theme across all abstracts, indicating its central role in AI-integrated education. Studies employ diverse methodologies, including experimental designs, qualitative analyses, and framework developments, with a focus on interdisciplinary applications. However, some abstracts lack detailed methods or results, as noted in quality issues, which may limit evidence extraction.
data.grounding_notes: Evidence is based solely on verbatim text from abstracts; quality notes indicate missing elements in some abstracts, so no inferences were made. All article keys are from the provided closed set, and quotes are exact copies from the abstracts.
